signals.entity: European Parliament / Council of the EU
signals.signal: TIMELINE SLIP CONFIRMED: the EP Legislative Observatory procedure file for the PSR (2023/0210(COD)) records the last completed step as 'Approval in committee of the text agreed at early 2nd reading interinstitutional negotiations' on 05/05/2026 (PE787.675), stage reached 'Awaiting Council's 1st reading position', and an INDICATIVE PLENARY SITTING DATE of 14/12/2026. No Council 1st-reading position, no signature and no Official Journal publication are recorded as of 02/08/2026 — contradicting the widely-repeated law-firm expectation of a June/July 2026 OJ publication. PSR = Payment Services Regulation (directly applicable EU law); PSD3 = the accompanying Third Payment Services Directive (needs national transposition).
signals.source_name: European Parliament Legislative Observatory (OEIL) — procedure file 2023/0210(COD)
signals.implies: The whole PSD3/PSR compliance clock moves right by roughly two quarters. If OJ publication lands Q1-2027, entry into force is ~Q1-2027+20 days and general application ~Q4-2028, with the Verification-of-Payee tail ~Q2-2029. For Printec this means the PSD3/PSR-driven refresh cycle (fraud/transaction monitoring — INETCO; AML/KYC — IMTF Siron, FICO; open-banking API hardening; SCA-accessible authentication at ATM/kiosk) is a FY2027 budget conversation, not FY2026. Printec should NOT pitch a hard 2028 deadline to Alpha Bank, BCR, Erste Croatia, Raiffeisen Serbia, OTP or Bank of Cyprus — the correct message this quarter is scoping/gap-assessment, not procurement.
signals.likelihood: High that Council 1st-reading position + EP plenary complete by end-Q1 2027; the 14/12/2026 sitting date is explicitly marked indicative/forecast
signals.followup: Re-check OEIL weekly for the Council 1st-reading position; the moment the OJ L reference appears, all 21/27-month dates become hard and every footprint bank's budget cycle opens.

signals.entity: Council of the EU — PSR final compromise text ST-8221/26
signals.country: EU (AT, BG, HR, CY, CZ, GR, HU, RO, SK, SI directly; RS/BA/MK/AL/XK/ME/UA by alignment)
signals.signal: VERIFICATION DEBT CLOSED — PSR Article 112 'Entry into force and application' in the final compromise text reads: the Regulation enters into force on the 20th day after OJ publication; 'It shall apply from [21 months after the date of entry into force]'; 'However, Articles 50 and 57 shall apply from [27 months after the date of entry into force]'; 'Articles 85a and 108a shall apply from the date of entry into force'. So the baseline's open question (18 vs 21 months general; 24 vs 27 months VoP tail) is settled at 21 and 27 months. Article 50 extends VoP (Verification of Payee — the payer's bank must check that the payee name matches the IBAN before the transfer is confirmed) to ALL credit transfers by applying Articles 5c(1)-(7) and 5b(2) of Regulation (EU) 260/2012 mutatis mutandis; Article 57 is the matching liability rule (the payer's PSP must refund without delay where a VoP failure causes a defectively executed transaction, and the payee's PSP or PISP must compensate the payer's PSP).
signals.source_name: Council of the EU, doc ST-8221-2026-INIT (PSR final compromise text, 428pp, ECOFIN.1.B, LIMITE) — Article 112
signals.implies: (a) Affected: every credit institution and payment institution in the 10 footprint EU states, plus EU-owned subsidiaries in RS/BA/MK/AL/XK/ME that align group-wide (Erste, RBI, OTP, UniCredit, NLB, ProCredit). (b) Must buy/change: VoP is currently a EURO-instant/SEPA obligation only — Article 50 extends the name-check to non-euro and non-instant credit transfers, i.e. BG/CZ/HU/RO domestic RTGS and ACH rails must be wired into a routing-and-verification mechanism. Printec sells into this via transaction monitoring (INETCO), core payment-channel integration and the ATM/kiosk front end where the near-match warning must be displayed. (c) Budget: the 27-month tail means commit 6-12 months ahead, i.e. roughly 15-21 months after OJ publication — on a Q1-2027 OJ that is H2-2028 spend, with scoping in 2027.
signals.likelihood: Certain once published; the 21/27-month split survived trilogue and is in the COREPER-endorsed text
signals.followup: Re-verify Article 112 against the OJ L text when published — the compromise text is LIMITE and the OP date placeholders are still unfilled.

signals.signal: PRIMARY-SOURCE TEXT OBTAINED. Article 59(-1) creates a NEW standalone obligation: 'Payment service providers shall have adequate prevention and robust technical safeguards in place to prevent cases where fraudsters replicate and misuse the payment service provider's communication channels'. Art 59(1): where a consumer was manipulated by a third party pretending to be their PSP using communication channels attributed to that PSP, the PSP must refund the FULL amount, conditional on the consumer notifying the PSP without undue delay and reporting to the police. Art 59(2): within 15 BUSINESS DAYS of being notified AND provided with the police report, the PSP must either refund or give a justified refusal (and signpost ADR/complaint bodies). Art 59(3): no refund where the consumer acted fraudulently or with gross negligence. Art 59(4): the BURDEN OF PROOF is on the PSP, which must first invite the consumer to explain the events, and the consumer's silence alone cannot found a gross-negligence finding. NOTE: the refund window is 15 business days, NOT the 10 business days recorded in the 24/07/2026 baseline — the baseline figure is CORRECTED.
signals.source_name: Council of the EU, doc ST-8221-2026-INIT (PSR final compromise text) — Article 59
signals.implies: (a) Affected: every retail bank in AT, BG, HR, CY, CZ, GR, HU, RO, SK, SI — and in practice their non-EU sister banks in RS/BA/MK/AL/XK/ME/UA, because group fraud policy is set centrally. (b) Must buy/change: three distinct spends. First, Art 59(-1) 'robust technical safeguards' against channel spoofing = brand/channel-impersonation defence, SMS-sender and caller-ID protection, and authenticated customer communications. Second, the 15-business-day clock plus reversed burden of proof forces an auditable, evidence-grade fraud case file per claim — that is real-time transaction monitoring with retained session evidence (INETCO), behavioural analytics (FICO), and AML/fraud case management (IMTF Siron). Third, banks that cannot prove gross negligence pay — so the ROI case for detection tooling is now a hard P&L number, not a compliance line. (c) Budget: 21 months after entry into force; commit 6-12 months earlier. On a Q1-2027 OJ this is procurement through 2027-H1 2028 for a Q4-2028 go-live.
signals.likelihood: High — Article 59 survived trilogue essentially intact and is the single most-cited PSR provision
signals.followup: Build a Printec one-pager quantifying refund exposure per 1,000 spoofing claims at 15-day settlement; lead with Alpha Bank (existing Siron account) and BCR. Note the burden-of-proof/gross-negligence assessment is a contested legal interpretation — refer any client-specific liability question to Printec Compliance/DPO rather than opining.

signals.entity: PSR Articles 59a and 59b — telco and online-platform secondary duties
signals.signal: The final text does NOT impose a direct monetary liability on telcos/platforms; it imposes DUTIES. Art 59a(-1): where payment fraud originates in fraudulent content published online, PSPs must without undue delay notify hosting providers under Art 16 (or Art 22) of the DSA, Regulation (EU) 2022/2065. Art 59a(1): data may be exchanged between PSPs and hosting providers, and between PSPs and providers of electronic communications services (Art 2(4)(b) of Directive (EU) 2018/1972 — the EECC), where there are objectively justified grounds to suspect fraud. Art 59a(2): ECSPs and providers of VLOPs/VLOSEs (Art 33 DSA) MUST establish dedicated communication channels with PSPs or join an information-sharing mechanism. Art 59a(5): ECSPs must take technical and organisational measures to detect and prevent impersonation fraud including calling-line-identification (CLI) and e-mail-address spoofing. Art 59b: VLOPs/VLOSEs must obtain an authorisation/registration number from every advertiser of a regulated financial service, make best efforts to verify it against the PSD3 registers using automated tools, and refuse the advertisement if the information is not obtained. Art 59a(4): the Commission and the European Board of Digital Services are to facilitate a voluntary EU code of conduct on payment fraud.
signals.source_name: Council of the EU, doc ST-8221-2026-INIT (PSR final compromise text) — Articles 59a, 59b
signals.implies: (a) Affected: footprint banks are on the PSP side of a new machine-to-machine fraud-intelligence exchange with telcos and platforms — in practice A1/Telekom Austria, Deutsche Telekom (HR/GR/MK/HU), Vodafone (GR/RO/HU), Telekom Srbija, Kyivstar. (b) Must buy/change: banks need an outbound fraud-signal interface and an inbound one — a fraud data-sharing hub with GDPR-safe minimisation, plus DSA Art 16 notice-and-action tooling. This maps to Printec's transaction monitoring (INETCO) and AML/case-management (IMTF Siron) as the system of record, and to integration/managed services to build the telco and platform connectors. It also creates a cross-industry consortium opportunity Printec is unusually placed to broker given it already sits inside both bank and retail estates across 17 markets. (c) Budget: same 21-month clock; the shared-channel build is a 2028 dependency that must be scoped in 2027 because it needs counterparties, not just software.
signals.likelihood: High that the duties land as drafted; Medium that a national shared fraud utility emerges in any single footprint market by 2029
signals.followup: The PSP-telco data exchange is personal-data processing under GDPR and ePrivacy (Directive 2002/58/EC is expressly preserved) — do NOT advise a client on the lawful basis; route to Printec's DPO / Compliance team.

signals.entity: PSR Articles 35, 38, 39 — open-banking API performance and the end of the fallback interface
signals.signal: The word 'fallback' does not appear in the final PSR text — the PSD2 permanent fallback interface is gone, replaced by a dedicated-interface regime with hard performance rules. Art 38(1): ASPSPs (account servicing PSPs, i.e. the banks) must limit planned unavailability and prevent unplanned unavailability; unavailability is PRESUMED where five consecutive access requests receive server errors or no response within 30 SECONDS. Art 38(2): at least ONE MONTH advance notice of planned downtime, which shall normally occur between 00:00 and 06:00. Art 38(2a): on unplanned downtime the ASPSP must inform TPPs of remediation and estimated fix time and ensure an 'optimal recovery time'. Art 38(2b): the dedicated interface must deliver availability and performance AT LEAST EQUAL to the bank's own customer authentication/communication interface. Art 38(5): EBA to deliver draft RTS on quarterly availability/performance statistics and their publication, and on the optimal recovery time standard, within NINE MONTHS of entry into force. Art 39: a competent authority may, on request, exempt an ASPSP from having a dedicated interface (using its customer interface instead, or exceptionally none at all), with EBA RTS on the exemption criteria taking account of size, turnover and payment volume.
signals.source_name: Council of the EU, doc ST-8221-2026-INIT (PSR final compromise text) — Articles 38, 39
signals.implies: (a) Affected: every ASPSP in the 10 footprint EU states — including the many small Greek, Cypriot, Croatian, Slovenian and Slovak cooperative/regional banks that met PSD2 with a thin API plus a fallback. Removing the fallback and requiring parity with the bank's own channel is a step change for exactly those institutions; Art 39 gives the small ones an exemption route worth applying for. (b) Must buy/change: API gateway uplift, synthetic monitoring against the 5-error/30-second presumption, published quarterly KPI reporting, and 24x7 monitoring with a defined recovery time. This is squarely Printec's device/service telemetry and monitoring practice extended to payment APIs, plus managed services (500+ engineers) for the 24x7 watch and the quarterly regulatory statistics pack. (c) Budget: the EBA RTS lands ~9 months after entry into force, so technical detail is knowable ~mid-2028 on a Q1-2027 OJ; banks that wait for the RTS will miss the 21-month date, so scoping money must be committed in 2027.
signals.followup: Track the EBA consultation on the Art 38(5) and Art 39(2) RTS — it will define the exact KPI thresholds that Printec's monitoring product must report against.

signals.entity: PSR Article 88 — accessibility requirements for strong customer authentication
signals.country: EU-wide (AT, BG, HR, CY, CZ, GR, HU, RO, SK, SI)
signals.signal: NEW, LARGELY UNREPORTED PROVISION. PSR Article 88 'Accessibility requirements regarding strong customer authentication': without prejudice to the European Accessibility Act (Directive (EU) 2019/882), PSPs must ensure that ALL customers — expressly including persons with disabilities, older persons, persons with low digital skills, and 'those who do not have access to digital channels or payment instruments' — have at their disposal at least ONE means, adapted to their situation, enabling them to perform SCA (Strong Customer Authentication — the two-factor check the bank must apply to electronic payments and account access), FREE OF CHARGE. Recital 110 ties this expressly to financial inclusion and to the EAA. Related: the PSR also requires EBA guidelines, due 18 months after entry into force, on how to assess that the independence of two 'inherence' (biometric) authentication elements is fully preserved.
signals.source_name: Council of the EU, doc ST-8221-2026-INIT (PSR final compromise text) — Article 88 and recital 110
signals.implies: (a) Affected: every PSP in the 10 footprint EU states, and disproportionately the high-cash, older-demographic markets — GR, BG, RO, HR, HU — where smartphone-only SCA excludes a large minority. (b) Must buy/change: banks must field a NON-SMARTPHONE SCA channel at zero customer cost. The practical answers are hardware tokens, card-reader/CAP devices, and — most relevant to Printec — SCA performed at the bank's own attended and self-service estate: ATMs, self-service kiosks and branch devices acting as an authentication point. This stacks directly on the EAA/EN 301 549 ATM accessibility workstream Printec is already selling (accessible ATM UI, audio jack, tactile keypad) and on Thales HSM / remote key injection for the cryptographic side. Selling Article 88 and the EAA as ONE accessible-self-service programme is the strongest combined pitch in the footprint. (c) Budget: 21 months after entry into force, so commit 6-12 months earlier; but the EAA has applied since 28/06/2025, so the accessible-terminal spend is ALREADY live and Article 88 should be used to enlarge an EAA business case now rather than to open a new 2028 one.
signals.followup: Pair this with the accessibility-eaa workstream row set; propose a single 'accessible authentication + accessible terminal' bundle to Bank of Cyprus, Alpha Bank and OTP.

signals.country: EU-wide; highest impact GR, HR, CY, BG, HU (independent ATM deployer / DCC-heavy markets)
signals.signal: The PSR closes the PSD2 ATM-operator loophole. Recital 9: the PSD2 exclusion for certain ATM operators 'has proven difficult to apply in practice' and is replaced by a new category of 'ATM deployers which do not service payment accounts', which become subject to REGISTRATION under PSD3 (referenced as Article 38 of [PSD3]) and to fee-transparency requirements. PSR Article 7 'Information requirements applicable to cash withdrawal services': any natural or legal person providing cash withdrawal services, including registered ATM deployers, must DISPLAY AT THE ATM the charges for the withdrawal payable by the customer, including conversion charges where applicable, in accordance with Article 5(4). PSD3/PSR also require currency-conversion charges at an ATM or POS to be expressed both as a monetary amount in the payer's account currency and as a percentage mark-up over an aggregated mid-market ECB reference rate.
signals.source_name: Council of the EU, doc ST-8221-2026-INIT (PSR final compromise text) — recital 9, Articles 5, 7
signals.implies: (a) Affected: independent ATM deployers (IADs) — Euronet and local operators in GR, HR, HU, CY, BG — plus every bank ATM that offers dynamic currency conversion. Tourist-heavy Greece, Croatia and Cyprus are the sharp end. (b) Must buy/change: an ATM software change, not a hardware change — the screen and receipt flow must render a mandated fee/mark-up disclosure computed against an ECB mid-market rate before the customer commits. That is precisely a multivendor ATM application change: Printec's x-core multivendor ATM software plus NCR APTRA screen-flow work, with the mark-up calculation as a configuration/pricing-service item. Newly registered IADs also acquire PSD3 registration, safeguarding and reporting obligations they have never had — a managed-compliance and monitoring services opening for Printec beyond its bank base. (c) Budget: 21 months after entry into force. ATM screen-flow programmes across a multi-hundred-terminal estate take 6-9 months, so commit ~12 months ahead.
signals.followup: Confirm the exact PSD3 article number for ATM-deployer registration from ST-8222-2026-INIT (the PSR cross-refers to 'Article 38 of [PSD3]'). Target Euronet Greece/Croatia and the Greek four systemic banks' DCC flows.

signals.entity: EBA (European Banking Authority) — PSR level-2 mandate calendar
signals.signal: The final PSR text sets EBA delivery deadlines all keyed to ENTRY INTO FORCE (not to application), so the level-2 work starts immediately on OJ publication: NINE MONTHS — RTS on dedicated-interface availability/performance quarterly statistics and on the optimal recovery time (Art 38(5)). ONE YEAR — RTS on the conditions for the Art 2(2)(j) scope exclusion; RTS on the harmonised format of the notification/motivation for refusing or withdrawing TPP access; RTS on the criteria justifying no interface at all (Art 39(2)); ITS on standard forms and templates for competent authorities to submit payment fraud data to EBA. 18 MONTHS — RTS specifying the data, methodology and periodicity of interface data provision to competent authorities; and EBA GUIDELINES on how to assess that the independence of two inherence (biometric) SCA elements is fully preserved. Plus EBA Guidelines on the commercial-agent exclusion and on complaints procedures (Art 90(1)), and an EBA report to the Commission on the application of sanctions.
signals.source_name: Council of the EU, doc ST-8221-2026-INIT (PSR final compromise text) — Articles 2, 38, 39, 88-89, 90, and mandate clauses
signals.implies: (a) Affected: all footprint EU PSPs plus their national competent authorities (OeNB/FMA, BNB, HNB, CBC, CNB, Bank of Greece, MNB, BNR, NBS-SK, Banka Slovenije). (b) Must buy/change: the payment-fraud-data ITS is the one with a direct product consequence — banks must report fraud statistics in an EBA-templated form to their NCA, which requires the fraud data to exist in a queryable, attributable store. That is a monitoring/reporting build (INETCO, Siron) rather than a policy exercise. The two-inherence-elements guideline matters for anyone planning biometric-only SCA on ATMs and kiosks. (c) Budget: no bank spend is triggered by the RTS themselves, but the nine-month API RTS is the earliest hard artefact and should anchor Printec's 2027 solution roadmap.
signals.likelihood: Certain that these mandates exist in the final text; timing depends entirely on the OJ date
signals.followup: Set a watch on eba.europa.eu consultation papers the month after OJ publication; the 9-month API RTS consultation will open first.

signals.entity: PSR Articles 85a and 108a — provisions applying from day one
signals.signal: Article 112 carves two provisions out of the 21-month clock and applies them FROM THE DATE OF ENTRY INTO FORCE (i.e. 20 days after OJ publication). Article 85a is an SCA derogation: by derogation from Article 85(1)(c), in the context of one or several RECURRING credit transfers initiated by the payer, SCA is not required for every instance. Article 108a is a transitional provision which, by derogation from PSD2 (Directive (EU) 2015/2366), governs the treatment of certain payment transactions until 21 months after entry into force. These are the only two substantive articles live on day one.
signals.source_name: Council of the EU, doc ST-8221-2026-INIT (PSR final compromise text) — Articles 85a, 108a, 112
signals.implies: (a) Affected: all footprint EU PSPs running standing orders and recurring credit transfers. (b) Must buy/change: the Art 85a derogation REDUCES friction — it lets banks drop repeat SCA on recurring credit transfers, which is a UX win rather than a spend, but it requires an authentication-engine rule change on day one of entry into force with no 21-month grace. Banks that ignore it simply keep over-authenticating; banks that adopt it need a controlled change to the SCA decisioning layer. (c) Budget: small, and it lands the moment the OJ appears — this is the earliest PSR-driven change request Printec can raise with clients, and a useful low-risk door-opener into the larger Article 59 conversation.
signals.followup: Read the full Art 85a and Art 108a text from ST-8221 to confirm the exact scope of the recurring-transfer derogation before advising clients.

signals.country: EU (AT, BG, HR, CY, CZ, GR, HU, RO, SK, SI)
signals.signal: BASELINE FIGURE CORRECTED. PSD3 Article 49 'Transposition' in the final compromise text reads: 'Member States shall adopt and publish, by ... [21 months after entry into force of this Directive] at the latest the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive' and 'They shall apply those measures from ... [21 months after entry into force of this Directive]'. The 24/07/2026 baseline and most law-firm notes still say 18 months. PSD3 and PSR therefore bite on the SAME day, 21 months after entry into force — there is no directive/regulation gap, and no national grace period beyond it.
signals.source_name: Council of the EU, doc ST-8222-2026-INIT (PSD3 final compromise text, ECOFIN.1.B, LIMITE) — Article 49
signals.implies: (a) Affected: the legislatures and NCAs of the 10 footprint EU states (OeNB/FMA, BNB, HNB, CBC, CNB, Bank of Greece, MNB, BNR, NBS-SK, Banka Slovenije) plus every authorised payment institution and e-money institution that must re-license. (b) Must buy/change: PSD3 merges the e-money and payment-institution regimes, so EMIs across the footprint face a re-authorisation with new safeguarding, ICT-resilience (DORA Chapter II is cross-referenced in the registration file) and professional-indemnity evidence. That is a compliance-documentation and ICT-evidence exercise Printec can support through document management and managed services, and it puts DORA-grade monitoring evidence on the critical path. (c) Budget: 21 months after entry into force, with national draft laws typically circulating 9-12 months ahead — so the first footprint transposition bills should appear roughly 9-12 months after the OJ date.
signals.followup: Watch for the first footprint transposition bill (historically HU and CZ move earliest, GR and BG latest); that bill is the trigger for national gold-plating, which is where Printec's spend usually comes from.

signals.entity: PSD3 Article 38 — registration regime for independent ATM deployers (IADs)
signals.country: EU-wide; sharpest in GR, HR, CY, HU, BG, RO (high IAD and tourist-DCC density)
signals.signal: PSD3 Article 38 'Services enabling cash withdrawals offered by ATM deployers not servicing payment accounts': such deployers 'shall not be subject to authorisation but shall register, before taking up activity, with the competent authority of the Member State where the cash withdrawal services are intended to be provided'. The registration file must include the Article 3(3) documentation set, a description of audit and organisational arrangements, and — critically — must 'indicate how the person registering will ensure a high level of digital operational resilience in accordance with Chapter II of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554' (DORA). Registration may be refused or revoked for non-compliance. Recital 63 explains the PSD2 Article 3(o) exclusion 'has proven difficult to apply due to its ambiguity'. GRANDFATHERING: deployers already operating under PSD2 Art 3(o) by 21 months after entry into force may continue WITHOUT registration until 27 months after entry into force; national registers must be updated one week after that date and the information passed to EBA.
signals.source_name: Council of the EU, doc ST-8222-2026-INIT (PSD3 final compromise text) — Article 38, recital 63, transitional provisions
signals.implies: (a) Affected: Euronet and the local independent ATM estates in Greece, Croatia, Hungary, Cyprus, Bulgaria and Romania — operators that have never been supervised entities. (b) Must buy/change: an IAD must now evidence DORA-grade ICT resilience for its ATM estate: device telemetry, incident detection and reporting, tested continuity. This is exactly Printec's ATM/device telemetry and monitoring product plus managed/field services (500+ engineers), sold to a buyer segment Printec has historically served commercially rather than as a compliance vendor. It also raises IAD operating cost, which improves the relative economics of bank-owned recycling ATMs (NCR recyclers, Glory/Sesami TCRs) — a second, indirect pitch to the banks. (c) Budget: registration bites at 21 months (new entrants) / 27 months (incumbents) after entry into force; DORA evidence takes 9-12 months to build, so commit ~12 months ahead.
signals.followup: Build an 'IAD registration readiness' bundle (telemetry + incident reporting + continuity evidence) and take it to Euronet's Greek and Croatian operations; cross-sell against the DORA workstream.

signals.entity: PSD3 Article 37 — cash at retail without a purchase
signals.country: EU-wide; highest strategic impact in RO, BG, GR, HR, HU (high-cash, thin rural ATM coverage)
signals.signal: PSD3 Article 37 'Services where cash is provided in retail stores without a purchase' obliges Member States to EXEMPT from the Directive retailers providing cash independently of any purchase, subject to three cumulative conditions: (a) the service is offered at the premises by a person selling goods or services as a regular occupation; (b) the amount of cash per withdrawal does not exceed EUR 150 or the national-currency equivalent; and (ba) 'the client's withdrawal is subject to strong customer authentication'. Member States may set a lower per-withdrawal limit but 'not lower than EUR 100'. Member States may also impose a daily per-account withdrawal limit, which 'shall not be lower than EUR 200'. Charges must be disclosed to the user before the cash is provided (Art 37(1b)). Recital: the EUR 150 cap exists to prevent unfair competition with ATM deployers and to stop shops running out of cash.
signals.source_name: Council of the EU, doc ST-8222-2026-INIT (PSD3 final compromise text) — Article 37 and recital
signals.implies: (a) Affected: grocery and fuel retail chains across the footprint, their acquirers, and — as a competitive threat — bank ATM estates in rural RO, BG, GR, HR and HU. (b) Must buy/change: TWO-SIDED for Printec. Opportunity: the SCA condition means cash-at-retail cannot be done on a plain card swipe — it needs an SCA-capable terminal and a controlled cash-out flow, i.e. Verifone/Castles POS terminals plus terminal management (TMS) and an acquirer-side flow build, sold to retailers and acquirers. Threat: every EUR 150 dispensed at a till is a withdrawal that does not happen at an ATM, weakening the low-volume rural ATM business case and, with it, the replacement cycle for NCR dispensers. The defensive counter-pitch to banks is cash optimisation (NCR APTRA OptiCash, already live at Erste Croatia) and recycling ATMs/TCRs that lower cost per rural transaction. (c) Budget: 21 months after entry into force for the legal framework, but retailers move on commercial logic — acquirer-side pilots are plausible from 2027 once national limits are set.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High that at least three footprint states set a limit below EUR 150 given AML sensitivity; High that the exemption itself applies
signals.followup: Model ATM-volume cannibalisation per footprint market before pitching OptiCash renewals; the national per-withdrawal and daily limits are the swing variable and will only be known at transposition.

signals.entity: Narodna banka Srbije (NBS) — Draft Law on Amendments to the Law on Payment Services
signals.signal: On 05/06/2026 the NBS published on its 'Nacrti' (drafts) register a Draft Law on Amendments and Supplements to the Law on Payment Services [Нацрт закона о изменама и допунама Закона о платним услугама], with public consultation open until 11/06/2026 (comments to kabinetguvernera@nbs.rs and platni.sistem@nbs.rs). The draft aligns Serbia with Regulation (EU) 2024/886 (the Instant Payments Regulation, which amends PSD2), Regulation (EU) 2021/1230 on cross-border payments, Regulation (EU) 260/2012 (SEPA) and Directive 98/26/EC on settlement finality. Published alongside it on the same register: a Draft Law on Amendments to the Law on Interbank Fees and Special Rules for Card Payment Transactions (28/05/2026, extending scope to international card transactions), a Draft Law on Credit Institutions (26/05/2026) and a Draft Law on Amendments to the Law on the NBS (05/06/2026) harmonising with the EU treaties 'particularly for the post-accession period'. NOTE: the draft does NOT implement PSD3 or the PSR — Serbia is deliberately one legislative generation behind, closing PSD2 + IPR first.
signals.source_name: Narodna banka Srbije — Нацрти (register of draft regulations), nbs.rs [NBS register of draft laws and regulations]
signals.implies: (a) Affected: all Serbian banks including Raiffeisen Serbia (existing Printec x-core customer) and AikBank (NCR recyclers), plus Serbian payment institutions. (b) Must buy/change: the immediate Serbian spend is IPR/SEPA-driven (instant rails, VoP-equivalent name checking, interchange-scope changes on card acquiring) — NOT PSD3 fraud liability. Printec should sell Serbia the instant-payments and card-acquiring stack now (POS + TMS, transaction monitoring), and hold the Article 59 fraud-liability pitch until the EU text is in the OJ, because Serbian law will only import it via a later amendment cycle. The parallel NBS Law amendment referencing 'the post-accession period' signals NBS is legislating on an accession trajectory, so PSD3/PSR alignment is a 2029-2031 question for Serbia. (c) Budget: the card-interchange and instant-payments changes are 2027 line items; PSD3-equivalent spend is beyond the planning horizon.
signals.likelihood: High that the draft is enacted in 2026-2027; Low that Serbia legislates PSD3/PSR-equivalent rules before 2029
signals.followup: Retrieve the adopted text from Službeni glasnik once published, and check whether NBS carried over any VoP or impersonation-fraud provision beyond the Reg 2024/886 minimum.

signals.entity: National Bank of Ukraine (NBU) — open banking framework
signals.signal: [STANDING — dated 2025] Ukraine has already built a PSD2-equivalent open-banking regime ahead of the EU's PSD3 cycle. Confirmed from the NBU's own Open Banking page: the Regulation on Open Banking in Ukraine, approved by NBU Board Resolution No. 80 of 25/07/2025; the Regulation on the Authorization Procedure for Providers of Non-financial Payment Services, Resolution No. 81 of 25/07/2025; and the Regulation on the Procedure for Using Electronic Trust Services when PSPs Obtain Access to Users' Accounts, Resolution No. 82 of 25/07/2025. ASPSPs (banks) 'must set up basic specialized interfaces (APIs) and ensure that third-party payment service providers (PISPs/AISPs) have continuous access to their users' accounts in real time' and must publish the technical specifications of every API on their own websites. TPPs must hold a qualified open-banking certificate from a qualified provider of electronic trust services (QPETS). SCA is governed separately by NBU Resolution No. 58 of 03/05/2023 and ICT security by Resolution No. 43 of 19/05/2021. Press (The Paypers, Asters) reports banks had to comply by 01/01/2026 and that NBU Board Resolution No. 32 of 31/03/2026 (effective 03/04/2026) simplified PISP payment-initiation detail requirements — the 2026 amendment is NOT confirmed on the NBU primary page opened this run.
signals.source_name: National Bank of Ukraine — Open Banking (official page, retrieved with a desktop User-Agent after a 403)
signals.implies: (a) Affected: all Ukrainian ASPSPs including PrivatBank (existing Printec NCR recycler customer) and Oschadbank. (b) Must buy/change: Ukrainian banks are already carrying a live API-availability and qualified-certificate obligation, which is the same technical surface the EU's PSR Article 38 will impose (availability/performance parity, published specs). Printec can sell API availability monitoring and the electronic-trust-services integration in Ukraine TODAY, on an in-force rule, rather than on a 2028 EU deadline — a rare case where the non-EU footprint is the nearer-term buyer. (c) Budget: already committed; the buying window is remediation and monitoring, not greenfield build.
signals.followup: Confirm NBU Resolution No. 32/2026 directly on bank.gov.ua (Ukrainian-language legislation register) — it is press-only at present and must not be restated as fact without the primary text.

signals.entity: Magyar Nemzeti Bank (MNB) — supervisory expectations on PSR readiness
signals.signal: [STANDING — dated 2025] Lóránt Varga, head of department at the MNB, set out at PayTechShow (15/04/2025) five areas where Hungarian payment providers must invest for the PSR: (1) tightening of the exemption regime, with the commercial-agent exclusion narrowed so that more merchants need a licence; (2) extension of the surcharging ban to all intra-EU credit transfers and direct debits; (3) reinforced open banking, with a mandatory dedicated interface to defined standards and a prohibition on blocking TPP access; (4) heavier PSP liability, including refunds for unauthorised transactions and automatic liability for impersonation fraud; and (5) real-time fraud prevention plus Verification of Payee. Hungarian coverage published April 2025 [Hungarian title: 'PSR – Új korszak a pénzforgalmi szolgáltatásokban: Milyen fejlesztésekkel készüljenek a magyar szereplők?' = 'PSR – A new era in payment services: what developments should Hungarian players prepare for?']. Separately, the MNB has published supervisory news relaying the EBA Opinion on new types of payment fraud and possible mitigations. NOTE: the one-business-day refund figure cited in Hungarian press relates to UNAUTHORISED transactions, not to the Article 59 impersonation-fraud regime, whose window is 15 business days in the final text.
signals.source_name: FinTechZone (HU) reporting MNB head of department Lóránt Varga at PayTechShow; MNB supervisory news page on the EBA payment-fraud Opinion
signals.implies: (a) Affected: OTP, Erste Hungary, K&H, Raiffeisen Hungary, MBH and the Hungarian payment-institution population. (b) Must buy/change: the MNB has effectively pre-announced its supervisory checklist, and items (3), (4) and (5) are all Printec-addressable — API monitoring, fraud/AML case management (Siron), real-time transaction monitoring (INETCO) and VoP integration. Hungary is also a market where the supervisor historically front-runs EU deadlines (cf. NIS2 audits), so a Hungarian gold-plated early mandate is a live possibility. (c) Budget: MNB's own advice was to start preparing in 2025; realistic Hungarian bank budget commitment is 2027 for a 2028-2029 deadline.
signals.likelihood: Medium that MNB issues a formal PSR readiness expectation or management circular before the OJ text exists
signals.followup: Check mnb.hu 'felugyeleti hirek' and any vezetoi korlevel (management circular) on PSR readiness — a formal MNB circular would convert this from a conference remark into a hard sales trigger. Only press-tier corroboration was found this run.

signals.entity: Footprint national competent authorities — PSD3/PSR transposition status
signals.country: Austria, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Greece, Hungary, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia (EU-10); Albania, Bosnia & Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Ukraine (non-EU-7)
signals.signal: GENUINE NIL RETURN, DELIBERATELY SEARCHED. No footprint national competent authority has opened PSD3 transposition work, published a consultation, or issued a PSD3/PSR readiness expectation as of 02/08/2026 — because the Directive has not been adopted and no OJ text exists to transpose. Searched this run: Bank of Greece supervision pages (only the PSD2 page exists, in Greek); BNR (Romanian, PSD3/fraud/refund terms — only press and a 2025 sector-reform commentary); HNB, Banka Slovenije and NBS-SK (nothing PSD3-specific); MNB (a 2025 conference remark and EBA-Opinion relays only, no circular); NBS Serbia's own Nacrti register (draft law implements Reg 2024/886, not PSD3); NBU Ukraine (a PSD2-equivalent open-banking regime, no PSD3 work). The only regulator-adjacent 2026 activity in the footprint that touches this file is Serbia's 05/06/2026 draft law and Ukraine's in-force open-banking rules — both one generation behind. Best available proxy for national timing: PSD3 Article 49 gives Member States 21 months from entry into force, and the historical PSD2 pattern in the footprint was that HU and CZ tabled bills first and GR and BG last (Greece missed the PSD2 deadline and Bulgaria transposed late).
signals.source_name: European Parliament Legislative Observatory (procedure file 2023/0210(COD)) plus targeted searches of Bank of Greece, BNR, HNB, BSI, NBS-SK, MNB, NBS-RS and NBU sites in Greek, Romanian, Hungarian, Serbian, Croatian and Ukrainian
signals.implies: (a) Affected: nothing yet — and that is the commercially important fact. (b) Must buy/change: no footprint bank has a PSD3/PSR line in its 2026 budget, and none can justify one to its board while the EP plenary date is still a forecast. (c) Budget: Printec's PSD3/PSR pipeline should be built as gap-assessment and advisory engagements in 2026, converting to product procurement in 2027-2028. The exception is the three items that stand on their own legs TODAY regardless of PSD3: EAA-driven accessible self-service (in force since 28/06/2025), instant-payments/VoP under Reg 2024/886, and DORA ICT resilience — all of which pre-build the PSD3/PSR technical surface and should be the vehicle for the conversation.
signals.likelihood: High that the first footprint transposition consultation appears 6-12 months after OJ publication, i.e. not before H2 2027 on current timing
signals.followup: Re-run the national sweep the month after OJ publication; the tell will be a finance-ministry consultation, not a central-bank one, in most footprint states.

signals.entity: European Parliament ECON committee chair vs. EP Legislative Observatory forecast
signals.signal: CONFLICTING TIMING SIGNALS, BOTH TRACEABLE. On 18/05/2026 the chair of the EP ECON committee wrote to the Council Presidency confirming that if the Council transmits its position on PSD3 and the PSR in its current form, ECON will recommend adoption at second reading WITHOUT amendment, and urged acceleration of the legal-linguistic finalisation so Parliament can adopt the package 'by September 2026 at the latest'. Against that, the EP's own Legislative Observatory still lists the file as 'Awaiting Council's 1st reading position' with an indicative plenary sitting date of 14/12/2026, and the Legislative Train entry (last updated 20/06/2026) says only that 'the deal needs to be formally adopted by Parliament and Council before it can enter into force', giving no dates. The binding constraint is the legal-linguistic revision of two texts running to roughly 430 and 250 pages in 24 languages.
signals.source_name: EP Legislative Train Schedule — Payment services regulation (primary, last update 20/06/2026); EP Legislative Observatory 2023/0210(COD) (primary); Bird & Bird and Norton Rose Fulbright notes on the 18/05/2026 ECON chair letter (press)
signals.implies: (a) Affected: Printec's own FY2027 sales planning more than any single bank. (b) Must buy/change: the spread between a September-2026 and a December-2026 plenary is a full quarter on every downstream date — general application moves between roughly Q3 2028 and Q1 2029, and the VoP tail between Q1 2029 and Q3 2029. (c) Budget: Printec should plan on the LATER date for pipeline forecasting and the EARLIER date for solution readiness, and should not publish a specific application date in customer-facing material until the OJ L number exists.
signals.likelihood: Medium that plenary adoption occurs in Q4 2026; the September-2026 target had already been missed at the time of writing (02/08/2026) in the sense that no Council 1st-reading position had been transmitted
signals.followup: The single highest-value watch item on this beat: the Council's first-reading position. It unlocks everything and can appear with little notice on an ECOFIN or any Council configuration's A-item list.

coverage_notes: FULL FRESH RESEARCH (the earlier 02/08/2026 attempt left only an empty stub for this slug; nothing was resumed). Angles used: (1) EU primary procedural sources - EP Legislative Observatory procedure file 2023/0210(COD) and the EP Legislative Train entry, which together established that the file is still 'Awaiting Council's 1st reading position' with an indicative plenary sitting of 14/12/2026 and NO Official Journal publication as of 02/08/2026, contradicting the law-firm consensus of a Q2/Q3 2026 OJ; (2) full local text extraction of both final compromise texts, Council ST-8221-2026-INIT (PSR, 428pp) and ST-8222-2026-INIT (PSD3), which closed three of the baseline's open verification debts and CORRECTED two baseline figures - PSR Article 59 gives 15 business days not 10, and PSD3 Article 49 gives 21 months' transposition not 18; PSR Article 112 confirms 21 months general application, 27 months for Articles 50 and 57 (VoP and VoP liability), and immediate application of Articles 85a and 108a; (3) provision-level sweep of the extracted texts for terms the baseline never covered, which surfaced four previously unreported Printec-relevant provisions: PSR Art 88 accessible SCA free of charge, PSR Art 7 mandatory at-ATM fee and FX mark-up display, PSD3 Art 38 IAD registration with a DORA Chapter II evidence requirement and 27-month grandfathering, and PSD3 Art 37 cash-at-retail without purchase capped at EUR 150 with mandatory SCA; (4) full EBA level-2 mandate inventory extracted from the PSR text (9-month API RTS, four 1-year mandates, two 18-month mandates, plus guidelines); (5) mandatory local-language footprint sweep in Greek, Romanian, Hungarian, Serbian, Croatian/Slovenian/Slovak and Ukrainian, plus the regulators' own pages - NBS Serbia's Nacrti register (primary, Serbian) yielded the 05/06/2026 draft Law on Payment Services implementing Reg 2024/886 rather than PSD3, and NBU Ukraine's Open Banking page (primary, retrieved with a desktop User-Agent after a 403) confirmed Resolutions 80/81/82 of 25/07/2025. GENUINE GAPS, honestly stated: (a) no footprint NCA has any PSD3/PSR transposition activity, which is reported as a nil-return signal with the search list and the Art 49 21-month proxy rather than omitted; (b) the OJ L reference and therefore all hard dates do not exist yet - every date in this file is expressed relative to entry into force, never as an invented calendar date; (c) the Hungarian MNB item rests on press coverage of a conference remark and is marked Low confidence and is_new=false; (d) the reported NBU Resolution No. 32 of 31/03/2026 amending the open-banking rules could not be confirmed on a primary NBU page and is flagged in the followup rather than asserted; (e) Bosnia & Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Albania produced nothing on this workstream, which is expected - none has begun PSD2-equivalent open-banking or payment-services alignment at a level where PSD3 is relevant, and their live payments file is the Western Balkans TIPS clone, covered by the instant-payments workstream.
